## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey or peer-reviewed study of the bottom was found.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best season.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Read directly: Wikipedia (Kirra and Snapper Rocks pages), Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, City of Gold Coast, National Surfing Reserves, WSL Secrets, Experience Gold Coast, Surf Atlas, TSB 1997 surf impact assessment, TSB Feb 2024 committee notes. GROYNE HISTORY conflicts: Wikipedia says the groyne was built in May 1972, while the 1997 government assessment says it was extended 400 m in 1974. For the 30 m removal, Wikipedia says 1995 and TSB 1997 says June 1996. Surf Atlas claims a 'later extension' of the groyne restored Kirra, which contradicts both. WIND: Surf-Forecast's 'best wind from the south' (180, at the +-45 boundary of the profile's 225) is the only single readable offshore direction; WannaSurf's SE contradicts it. The Surfing Reserves window (SE/S/SW) and TSB 1997's regional statement that winter SW-NW winds are offshore both contain 225. No readable source names SW explicitly for Kirra. SWELL DIRECTION: SE consensus (Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, Surfing Reserves E/SE). Experience Gold Coast and Surf Atlas say S-SE, extending up to 30 deg south of the profile optimum max of 150, so consider widening the optimum to ~165. SIZE: WannaSurf starts at 5-6 ft and holds 8 ft+. TSB 1997 gives 1-3 m (pre-1974 classic ride) and 2-4 m near the surfability limit. The council and Experience Gold Coast say it needs big swells. The profile's 3-12 ft fits the upper end; a 3 ft minimum looks low against WannaSurf's 5 ft. PERIOD: no source. TIDE: WSL's 'solid swell and low tide' supports low_to_mid; Surf-Forecast says tide doesn't matter. SEASON: Surf-Forecast autumn-winter and Surf Atlas winter-and-fall overlap the profile only in Mar-May; Surf Atlas's winter-spring 'sweet spot' contradicts it. The profile's Jan-Feb has no readable support. RECENCY: Kirra's quality has suffered since the Superbank (Wikipedia). TSB notes read but not recorded (Aug 2019, Nov 2019, Feb 2020) mention a dissipated bank, a lagoon and limited surfing. Feb 2024 says Kirra was a fun longboard wave. No measured bathymetry dataset was read.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 5–6 ft [S4] · 3.3 ft [S10] | conflicting | S4, S5, S8, S10 | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | — | not documented | — | no separate setting; working range 3–12 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 8–9.8 ft | documented | S4, S10 | `wave_height_max_ft` 12 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.5-2 m / 5-6 ft, while the 1997 Tweed Sand Bypassing assessment describes the ride in waves from 1 to 3 m (1 x 3.28 = 3.3 ft; the researcher's claim says this was the pre-1974 ride); City of Gold Coast and Experience Gold Coast say it needs big or large swells, without numbers.
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 2.5m+ / 8ft+”
  - S10 (Tweed Sand Bypassing (NSW and Qld Governments)): “The ride, a right peel with an angle of about 35 degrees and waves fiom 1 to 3 m”
  - S5 (City of Gold Coast): “is a popular with experienced board riders when big swells are running, producing a long, hollow, barrelling wave”
  - S8 (Experience Gold Coast (tourism)): “The rest of the time, Kirra is generally a slower wave and a relaxed spot”
- **Ideal range**: No excerpt states an ideal or best size range.
- **Maximum suitable**: WannaSurf's top bracket is 2.5 m+ / 8 ft+ (open-ended) and the 1997 assessment gives waves up to 3 m (3 x 3.28 = 9.8 ft); neither states a true upper limit or whether the heights are face or offshore.
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 2.5m+ / 8ft+”
  - S10 (Tweed Sand Bypassing (NSW and Qld Governments)): “The ride, a right peel with an angle of about 35 degrees and waves fiom 1 to 3 m”

Notes:

- **Ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast gives southeast as the ideal swell direction, WannaSurf lists southeast as good, and National Surfing Reserves says the best conditions are an E/SE swell; SE = 135 deg.
  - S3 (Surf-Forecast.com): “the ideal swell direction is from the southeast”
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Good swell directionSouthEast”
  - S6 (National Surfing Reserves (surfingreserves.org)): “The best conditions are E/SE swell with SE/S/SW winds.”
- **Acceptable range**: National Surfing Reserves gives E/SE (90-135 deg) and Experience Gold Coast and Surf Atlas say large or winter S-SE swells fire Kirra (135-180 deg); the value spans both.
  - S6 (National Surfing Reserves (surfingreserves.org)): “The best conditions are E/SE swell with SE/S/SW winds.”
  - S8 (Experience Gold Coast (tourism)): “When the sand is right and large south/south-east swells awaken Kirra, you can expect to see some of the world's best tube riding.”
  - S9 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “When the winter S-SE swells come curling into the bays past Snapper Rocks”
- **Blocked directions**: No excerpt names swell directions that are blocked or shadowed by land or reefs.
- **Exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls Kirra a very sheltered point/groyne break with fairly consistent surf, and National Surfing Reserves says Kirra is more exposed to the SE swell-line wrap, with a bigger wave than the inner bays.
  - S3 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Kirra on the Gold Coast is a very sheltered point/Groyne break that has fairly consistent surf.”
  - S6 (National Surfing Reserves (surfingreserves.org)): “More exposed to the SE swell line wrap and has a bigger wave size as the swell evens out.”

  - S1 (Wikipedia): “Today sand pumping across the Tweed River mouth has filled it in and changed its character.”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.5-2 m / 5-6 ft, while the 1997 Tweed Sand Bypassing assessment describes the ride in waves from 1 to 3 m (1 x 3.28 = 3.3 ft; the researcher's claim says this was the pre-1974 ride); City of Gold Coast and Experience Gold Coast say it needs big or large swells, without numbers.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast gives south as the best wind (its conditions line calls it offshore), WannaSurf lists southeast as good and National Surfing Reserves SE, S and SW as best, while the 1997 assessment says the region's winter winds are mainly southwest to northwest and offshore; SE and SW-NW are far apart.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: WSL says its old glory comes alight with a solid swell and low tide, while Surf-Forecast says the quality of the surf is not affected by the tide.
